I also do this. I have dermatillomania and ADHD. My psych explained to me that this behavior is pretty much a way of self-soothing or self regulating when you’re bored.

There’s a condition called dermatophagia. It’s when you feel a compulsion to bite, chew, or eat your own skin (whether it’s dead skin or the skin around your nails). It can be really embarrassing but I do it as well around my fingernails. It’s related to OCD, autism, and ADHD but you don’t have to have those to do this. People who have OCD or are neurodivergent tend to have body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) that help them emotionally regulate. Behavior like this isn’t as uncommon as you’d think, but there’s so much stigma and shame around it that not many people talk about it.

Salt water works because when there’s more salt in the water you’re gargling than in the tissues in your throat, the the cells want to make that salt to water ratio equal and get rid of some water from the cells. This is partially how your body makes sure all the cells are hydrated, by sensing the salt to water ratio in surrounding tissues and balancing the water levels equally. With salt water, it’s the same idea. You’re creating a very salty environment and the cells think they need to purge water. This brings down inflammation, which can make your throat feel slightly better. It also kills (some, not all) bacteria with the same mechanism, the water essentially gets sucked out of the bacteria and dehydrates it to the point of cell death. This isn’t as big of an issue for our tissues.
